hindi_devanagari: नमस्ते!
hindi_roman: Namaste!
english_meaning: Hello / Greetings!
grammar_note: Marathi commonly uses 'नमस्कार' (Namaskar) for general respectful greeting.
context_note: Appropriate in formal, semi-formal, and informal settings.
common_mistakes: Using casual slang with elders; stick to Namaskar/Namaste.

hindi_devanagari: सुप्रभात!
hindi_roman: Suprabhat!
english_meaning: Good morning!
grammar_note: Marathi prefers 'शुभ सकाळ' (sakaal = morning) directly over Sanskritized Suprabhat in daily speech.

hindi_devanagari: शुभ रात्रि!
hindi_roman: Shubh raatri!
english_meaning: Good night!
grammar_note: Shared Sanskrit origin; identical in both languages.
context_note: Used when departing at night or going to bed.

hindi_devanagari: आप कैसे हैं?
hindi_roman: Aap kaise hain?
english_meaning: How are you? (Formal/Elder)
grammar_note: Honorific 2nd person plural 'तुम्ही' requires auxiliary 'आहात', matching Hindi 'आप ... हैं'.
context_note: Always use with elders, teachers, or in business contexts.
common_mistakes: Addressing an elder with informal 'तू' (tu).

hindi_devanagari: तुम कैसे हो?
hindi_roman: Tum kaise ho?
english_meaning: How are you? (Informal male)
grammar_note: Informal question inflects for gender in Marathi: 'कसा' for male, 'कशी' for female.
context_note: Used between close friends or to younger individuals.
common_mistakes: Using masculine 'कसा' when addressing a female friend (use 'कशी आहेस').

hindi_devanagari: सब ठीक है?
hindi_roman: Sab theek hai?
english_meaning: Is everything alright?
grammar_note: Marathi adds the interrogative particle 'का' (ka) at the end of yes/no questions.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the question particle 'का' at the end of yes/no queries.

hindi_devanagari: फिर मिलेंगे!
hindi_roman: Phir milenge!
english_meaning: See you again!
grammar_note: Marathi verb 'भेटणे' (to meet) in 1st person plural hortative form 'भेटू'.
context_note: Standard farewell phrase among friends and colleagues.

hindi_devanagari: अलविदा!
hindi_roman: Alvida!
english_meaning: Goodbye! (lit: I will take leave)
grammar_note: In Maharashtrian culture, saying 'जातो' (I am going) is considered inauspicious; speakers say 'येतो' (male) or 'येते' (female) meaning 'I will return'.
common_mistakes: Saying literal 'मी जातो' instead of customary 'मी येतो'.
Saying 'अलविदा' which sounds melodramatic.

hindi_devanagari: मेरा नाम राहुल है।
hindi_roman: Mera naam Rahul hai.
english_meaning: My name is Rahul.
grammar_note: In Marathi 'नाव' (name) is neuter gender, so possessive pronoun becomes neuter 'माझं' (mazha).
common_mistakes: Using masculine 'माझा नाव' instead of neuter 'माझं नाव'.

hindi_devanagari: तुम्हारा नाम क्या है?
hindi_roman: Tumhara naam kya hai?
english_meaning: What is your name?
grammar_note: Neuter agreement applies: 'तुझं नाव'. Interrogative 'what' is 'काय' (kay).

hindi_devanagari: आपका नाम क्या है?
hindi_roman: Aapka naam kya hai?
english_meaning: What is your name? (Respectful)
grammar_note: Honorific possessive 'तुमचं' (tumcha).
context_note: Use with strangers, clients, or elders.

hindi_devanagari: मैं मुंबई से हूँ।
hindi_roman: Main Mumbai se hoon.
english_meaning: I am from Mumbai.
grammar_note: Marathi uses ablative suffix '-हून' or '-वरून' directly attached to place names ('मुंबईहून' = from Mumbai).
common_mistakes: Using separate word like Hindi 'se' instead of the attached suffix '-हून'.

hindi_devanagari: मैं एक छात्र हूँ।
hindi_roman: Main ek chhatra hoon.
english_meaning: I am a student.
grammar_note: Marathi auxiliary for 1st person present is 'आहे' (same form as 3rd person).

hindi_devanagari: आपसे मिलकर खुशी हुई।
hindi_roman: Aapse milkar khushi hui.
english_meaning: Pleased to meet you.
grammar_note: Marathi verb 'होणे' (to happen/become) in past tense is 'झाला'. Dative 'तुम्हाला' is used.
common_mistakes: Translating Hindi 'खुशी' literally instead of Marathi 'आनंद झाला'.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे कल कॉलेज जाना है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe kal college jaana hai.
english_meaning: I have to go to college tomorrow.
grammar_note: Key contrast: Marathi 'उद्या' specifically means tomorrow. Dative destination takes '-ला'.
common_mistakes: Using 'काल' (which means yesterday) instead of 'उद्या' for tomorrow.
Omitting the '-ला' suffix on college.

hindi_devanagari: मेरी क्लास नौ बजे शुरू होती है।
hindi_roman: Meri class nau baje shuru hoti hai.
marathi_devanagari: माझा तास नऊ वाजता सुरू होतो।
marathi_roman: Mazha taas nau vaajta suru hoto.
english_meaning: My lecture starts at nine o'clock.
grammar_note: Time specification in Marathi adds '-ता' ('वाजता') to the numeral.
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'baje' instead of Marathi 'वाजता'.

hindi_devanagari: क्या तुमने असाइनमेंट पूरा किया?
hindi_roman: Kya tumne assignment poora kiya?
english_meaning: Did you complete the assignment?
grammar_note: Interrogative 'का' is placed clause-finally in Marathi.
common_mistakes: Placing 'का' at the beginning of the sentence like Hindi 'क्या'.

hindi_devanagari: लाइब्रेरी कहाँ है?
hindi_roman: Library kahan hai?
english_meaning: Where is the library?
grammar_note: Hindi interrogative locative 'कहाँ' corresponds directly to Marathi 'कुठे' (kuthe).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'kaha' in Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: आज प्रोफेसर छुट्टी पर हैं।
hindi_roman: Aaj professor chhutti par hain.
english_meaning: The professor is on leave today.
grammar_note: Marathi locative postposition '-वर' (on/upon) attaches directly to 'सुट्टी' -> 'सुट्टीवर'.

hindi_devanagari: किताब खोलो।
hindi_roman: Kitaab kholo.
english_meaning: Open the book.
grammar_note: Marathi verb 'उघडणे' (to open). Honorific imperative ends in '-ा' ('उघडा').

hindi_devanagari: कृपया ध्यान से सुनो।
hindi_roman: Kripya dhyan se suno.
english_meaning: Please listen carefully.
grammar_note: Marathi verb for hearing/listening is 'ऐकणे' (aikne), imperative 'ऐका' (aika).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'suno' instead of Marathi 'aika'.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे एक सवाल पूछना है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe ek sawaal poochhna hai.
english_meaning: I want to ask a question.

vocabulary.meaning: want to ask (masculine agreement with प्रश्न)

grammar_note: Marathi verb for asking is 'विचारणे' (vicharne); agrees with masculine 'प्रश्न' -> 'विचारायचा'.
common_mistakes: Using literal Hindi verb root 'poochhne'.

hindi_devanagari: क्या मैं अंदर आ सकता हूँ?
hindi_roman: Kya main andar aa sakta hoon?
english_meaning: May I come in?
grammar_note: Hindi 'अंदर' (andar) translates to Marathi 'आत' (aat).
common_mistakes: Saying 'andar' instead of 'aat'.

hindi_devanagari: चल, चाय पीने चलते हैं।
hindi_roman: Chal, chai peene chalte hain.
english_meaning: Come on, let's go have tea.
grammar_note: Tea is masculine in Marathi ('चहा छान आहे'), but feminine in Hindi ('चाय अच्छी है').
common_mistakes: Treating 'चहा' as feminine in Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: तू कहाँ गायब था?
hindi_roman: Tu kahan gayab tha?
english_meaning: Where were you vanished/missing?
grammar_note: 2nd person past singular for male in Marathi takes suffix '-स' ('होतास').

hindi_devanagari: मजाक मत कर यार।
hindi_roman: Mazaak mat kar yaar.
english_meaning: Don't joke, buddy.
grammar_note: Negative imperative 'don't' in Marathi is formed with auxiliary 'नको' / 'नकोस'.
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'mat' instead of Marathi 'nako'.

hindi_devanagari: हम सब साथ में पढ़ाई करेंगे।
hindi_roman: Hum sab saath mein padhai karenge.
english_meaning: We will all study together.
grammar_note: Marathi distinguishes inclusive 'आपण' (including listener) from exclusive 'आम्ही' (excluding listener).
common_mistakes: Confusing inclusive 'आपण' and exclusive 'आम्ही'.

hindi_devanagari: यह मेरी माँ है।
hindi_roman: Yeh meri maa hai.
english_meaning: This is my mother.
grammar_note: Mother in Marathi is 'आई' (Aai). Proximal demonstrative feminine is 'ही' (hee).
common_mistakes: Calling mother 'माताजी' or 'Maa' instead of customary 'आई'.

hindi_devanagari: मेरे पिता जी डॉक्टर हैं।
hindi_roman: Mere pita ji doctor hain.
english_meaning: My father is a doctor.
grammar_note: Father in Marathi is respectfully referred to as 'वडील' (vadeel) with plural agreement 'माझे'.
common_mistakes: Using singular agreement for father.

hindi_devanagari: मेरा एक छोटा भाई है।
hindi_roman: Mera ek chhota bhai hai.
english_meaning: I have a younger brother.

vocabulary.meaning: I have a brother (dative possessive construction)

grammar_note: Expressing possession of kin in Marathi uses dative 'मला ... आहे', unlike Hindi nominative 'मेरा ... है'.
common_mistakes: Using nominative 'माझा एक भाऊ आहे' instead of dative 'मला एक भाऊ आहे'.

hindi_devanagari: मेरी बड़ी बहन पुणे में रहती है।
hindi_roman: Meri badi behen Pune mein rehti hai.
english_meaning: My elder sister lives in Pune.
grammar_note: Locative in Marathi inflects the place noun directly with suffix '-त' ('पुण्यात', 'मुंबईत').
common_mistakes: Saying 'Pune mein' instead of locative 'पुण्यात'.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे बहुत भूख लगी है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe bahut bhookh lagi hai.
english_meaning: I am feeling very hungry.
grammar_note: Both languages use dative subject ('मला' / 'मुझे') with feminine noun 'भूक'.
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'bahut' instead of Marathi 'khoop'.

hindi_devanagari: खाना बहुत स्वादिष्ट है।
hindi_roman: Khana bahut swadisht hai.
english_meaning: The food is very delicious.
grammar_note: Food/meal is 'जेवण' (jevan). 'खूप छान आहे' is the most natural compliment.

hindi_devanagari: क्या आपको तीखा खाना पसंद है?
hindi_roman: Kya aapko teekha khana pasand hai?
english_meaning: Do you like spicy food?
grammar_note: Verb 'आवडणे' (to like) requires dative subject 'तुम्हाला' and agrees with object 'जेवण' -> 'आवडतं'.
common_mistakes: Saying 'pasand aahe' instead of authentic 'aavadta'.

hindi_devanagari: कृपया थोड़ा पानी दीजिए।
hindi_roman: Kripya thoda paani deejie.
english_meaning: Please give some water.
grammar_note: In Marathi, 'पाणी' (water) is grammatically neuter, hence 'थोडं पाणी' (thoda paani).
common_mistakes: Saying masculine 'थोडा पाणी' instead of neuter 'थोडं पाणी'.

hindi_devanagari: इसका दाम कितना है?
hindi_roman: Iska daam kitna hai?
english_meaning: How much does this cost?
grammar_note: Marathi interrogative quantity 'किती' (kiti) corresponds to Hindi 'कितना'.
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'kitna' in Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: बहुत महँगा है, थोड़ा कम करो।
hindi_roman: Bahut mehnga hai, thoda kam karo.
marathi_devanagari: खूप महाग आहे, थोडं कमी करा।
marathi_roman: Khoop mahaag aahe, thoda kami kara.
english_meaning: It is very expensive, reduce a bit.
grammar_note: Bargaining phrase: 'महाग' (mahaag) = expensive, 'कमी करा' (kami kara) = reduce.

hindi_devanagari: क्या आपके पास दूसरा रंग है?
hindi_roman: Kya aapke paas doosra rang hai?
english_meaning: Do you have another colour?
grammar_note: Possession in Marathi uses suffix '-कडे' ('तुमच्याकडे' = at you / with you).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'paas' instead of Marathi '-kade'.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे एक बिल दीजिए।
hindi_roman: Mujhe ek bill deejie.
english_meaning: Please give me the bill.
grammar_note: Dative subject 'मला' + imperative 'द्या'.

hindi_devanagari: रेलवे स्टेशन कितनी दूर है?
hindi_roman: Railway station kitni door hai?
english_meaning: How far is the railway station?
grammar_note: Marathi uses 'लांब' (laamb) for physical spatial distance where Hindi uses 'दूर' (door).
common_mistakes: Saying 'door aahe' instead of natural 'laamb aahe'.

hindi_devanagari: यह बस पुणे जाएगी क्या?
hindi_roman: Yeh bus Pune jaayegi kya?
english_meaning: Will this bus go to Pune?

vocabulary.meaning: will go to Pune (dative -ला + 3rd person future)

grammar_note: Destination takes dative postposition '-ला' ('पुण्याला'). Future 3rd person singular verb ends in '-ईल' ('जाईल').
common_mistakes: Omitting the destination marker '-ला'.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे दादर के लिए दो टिकट चाहिए।
hindi_roman: Mujhe Dadar ke liye do ticket chahiye.
english_meaning: I need two tickets for Dadar.
grammar_note: Marathi plural object ('तिकीटं') causes modal 'पाहिजे' to take plural ending 'पाहिजेत' (pahijet).
common_mistakes: Using singular 'पाहिजे' when asking for multiple items.

hindi_devanagari: अगला स्टॉप कौन सा है?
hindi_roman: Agla stop kaun sa hai?
english_meaning: Which is the next stop?
grammar_note: Spatial/temporal 'next' is 'पुढचा' (pudhcha). Interrogative 'which' is 'कोणता' (konta).

hindi_devanagari: सीधे जाइए और फिर दाएँ मुड़िए।
hindi_roman: Seedhe jaaiye aur phir daayein mudiye.
marathi_devanagari: सरळ जा आणि मग उजवीकडे वळा।
marathi_roman: Saral ja aani mag ujveekade vala.
english_meaning: Go straight and then turn right.
grammar_note: Right = 'उजवीकडे' (ujveekade), Left = 'डावीकडे' (daaveekade). Straight = 'सरळ' (saral).
common_mistakes: Confusing right ('उजवीकडे') and left ('डावीकडे').

hindi_devanagari: बाएँ हाथ पर एक मंदिर है।
hindi_roman: Baayein haath par ek mandir hai.
marathi_devanagari: डाव्या बाजूला एक देऊळ / मंदिर आहे।
marathi_roman: Daavya baajula ek deool / mandir aahe.
english_meaning: There is a temple on the left side.
grammar_note: Side is 'बाजू' (baaju), taking locative '-ला'.

hindi_devanagari: मेट्रो स्टेशन यहाँ से पास में है।
hindi_roman: Metro station yahan se paas mein hai.
english_meaning: Metro station is near from here.
grammar_note: Ablative 'from here' is contracted to 'इथून' (ithun) in Marathi. 'Near' is 'जवळ' (javal).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'paas' instead of Marathi 'javal'.

hindi_devanagari: मैं रोज़ सुबह छह बजे उठता हूँ।
hindi_roman: Main roz subah chhah baje uthta hoon.
marathi_devanagari: मी रोज सकाळी सहा वाजता उठतो।
marathi_roman: Mi roz sakaali saha vaajta uthto.
english_meaning: I wake up every day at six in the morning.
grammar_note: Marathi 1st person masculine present habitual verb ends in '-तो' ('उठतो').
common_mistakes: Female speakers should use '-ते' ('उठते').

hindi_devanagari: मैं रात को दस बजे सोता हूँ।
hindi_roman: Main raat ko das baje sota hoon.
english_meaning: I sleep at ten in the night.
grammar_note: Marathi verb for sleeping is 'झोपणे' (jhopne), distinct from Hindi 'सोना' (sona).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi root 'sota' in Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: मैं नाश्ते में पोहा खाता हूँ।
hindi_roman: Main naashte mein poha khaata hoon.
english_meaning: I eat poha for breakfast.
grammar_note: In Marathi, 'पोहे' (pohe) is grammatically plural. Locative 'नाश्त्यात' has oblique stem 'नाश्त्या-'.
common_mistakes: Treating 'pohe' as singular.

hindi_devanagari: कृपया मेरी मदद कीजिए।
hindi_roman: Kripya meri madad keejie.
english_meaning: Please help me.
grammar_note: Help recipient takes dative case 'मला' in Marathi, paired with polite imperative 'करा' (kara).
common_mistakes: Using nominative 'माझी मदत करा'.

hindi_devanagari: क्या आप यह फिर से बता सकते हैं?
hindi_roman: Kya aap yeh phir se bata sakte hain?
marathi_devanagari: तुम्ही हे पुन्हा सांगू शकता का?
marathi_roman: Tumhi he punha saangu shakta ka?
english_meaning: Can you tell this again?
grammar_note: Marathi verb for telling/saying is 'सांगणे' (saangne), potential form 'सांगू शकता'.
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'bataana'.

hindi_devanagari: एक मिनट रुकिए।
hindi_roman: Ek minute rukie.
english_meaning: Wait for a minute.
grammar_note: Marathi verb for waiting/stopping is 'थांबणे' (thaambne), imperative 'थांबा' (thaamba).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'ruko' instead of Marathi 'thaamba'.

hindi_devanagari: यह क्या है?
hindi_roman: Yeh kya hai?
english_meaning: What is this?
grammar_note: General pronoun 'this' for unknown object defaults to neuter 'हे' (he) in Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: वह कौन है?
hindi_roman: Vah kaun hai?
english_meaning: Who is he / she?
grammar_note: Interrogative 'who' is 'कोण' (kon). 3rd person pronouns distinguish gender ('तो' male, 'ती' female).

hindi_devanagari: आप कब आओगे?
hindi_roman: Aap kab aaoge?
english_meaning: When will you come?
grammar_note: Interrogative time word 'when' is 'कधी' (kadhi). Prospective form 'येणार' expresses expected future action.
common_mistakes: Using Hindi 'kab'.

hindi_devanagari: आप ऐसा क्यों कह रहे हैं?
hindi_roman: Aap aisa kyon keh rahe hain?
english_meaning: Why are you saying like this?
grammar_note: Interrogative 'why' is 'का' (ka) in Marathi. Verb for saying is 'म्हणणे' (mhan-ne).
common_mistakes: Confusing question-final 'का' (yes/no marker) with question 'का' (why).

hindi_devanagari: मुझे बहुत खुशी हो रही है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe bahut khushi ho rahi hai.
english_meaning: I am feeling very happy.
grammar_note: Mental state expressions use dative subject 'मला' + noun 'आनंद' + continuous auxiliary 'होत आहे'.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे आज बहुत थकान महसूस हो रही है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe aaj bahut thakaan mehsoos ho rahi hai.
marathi_devanagari: मला आज खूप थकवा जाणवतो आहे।
marathi_roman: Mala aaj khoop thakva jaanavto aahe.
english_meaning: I am feeling very tired today.
grammar_note: 'थकवा' (thakva) is masculine in Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: मुझे गुस्सा आ रहा है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe gussa aa raha hai.
english_meaning: I am feeling angry.
grammar_note: In Marathi, anger is 'राग' (raag). The idiom is 'राग येणे' (anger coming to dative subject).
common_mistakes: Using Hindi word 'gussa' in formal Marathi.

hindi_devanagari: अरे, क्या चल रहा है?
hindi_roman: Arre, kya chal raha hai?
english_meaning: Hey, what's going on?

vocabulary.meaning: what is going on (contracted colloquial continuous)

grammar_note: Contraction: 'चालले आहे' is colloquially spoken as 'चाललंय' (chaallay). Very common slang.
common_mistakes: Over-formalizing casual banter with 'काय चालले आहे' instead of natural 'काय चाललंय'.

hindi_devanagari: कुछ खास नहीं, बस वही सब।
hindi_roman: Kuchh khaas nahi, bas wahi sab.
english_meaning: Nothing special, just the usual.
grammar_note: Idiomatic response: 'तेच नेहमीचं' (tech nehmicha = the same habitual thing).

hindi_devanagari: तू सच बोल रहा है क्या?
hindi_roman: Tu sach bol raha hai kya?
english_meaning: Are you telling the truth?
grammar_note: Truth is 'खरं' (khara). Colloquial continuous: 'बोलत आहेस' contracts to 'बोलतोयस'.
